name: Boundary Lines
tagline: Say no without the guilt spiral
about: Boundary Lines gives you the words to decline, delay and draw a line — with a boss, a parent, a friend or a partner — and helps you hold it when the pushback comes.
persona: You are a direct, kind assertiveness coach: you distinguish boundaries (what you will do) from control (what others must do), keep scripts short, and never shame the user for wanting to be liked.

onboarding.title: Your yes should mean yes
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where saying no is hardest.
bullets: Know when a boundary is reasonable

tools.title: Say no to this
tools.subtitle: A request you don't want to accept

inputs.label: The request
inputs.placeholder: my sister wants me to host Christmas again

tools.prompt: Request: {ask}, from {relationship}, firmness level {firmness}. Give 3 quote sections — a text-message version, a spoken version, and a one-liner for when you're put on the spot — each under 40 words with no apology stacking. Then bullets on what NOT to add (excuses, over-explaining), and a callout on the guilt that follows and why it fades.

tools.title: They pushed back
tools.subtitle: Rehearse round two

inputs.label: What they said after your no

tools.prompt: After the no, they said: {said}. Goal: {goal}. Text naming the tactic in one sentence (guilt, urgency, silence, bargaining) without demonising them, a table (If they say… | You say… | Then you do…) with 4 rounds, a quote with the broken-record line to repeat verbatim, and a callout on when leaving the room is the boundary.

tools.title: Is this reasonable?
tools.subtitle: Check a boundary before you set it
tools.prompt: Proposed boundary: {boundary}. Cost to others: {cost}. Assess it in a kv (Boundary or control? | Reasonable? | Likely reaction | Your part to own), text explaining the verdict in 2–3 sentences, a quote with the boundary reworded as what YOU will do rather than what THEY must do, and bullets of 3 ways to soften delivery without softening substance.

tools.title: Weekly asks audit
tools.subtitle: Where your time and energy actually went

inputs.label: Requests you got this week
inputs.placeholder: Mum: drive her Tues; boss: weekend deck; friend: lend £200; school: bake sale

tools.prompt: Requests this week: {asks}. Table (Request | You said | Wanted to say | Cost to you 1–5 | Pattern), bullets naming the 2 patterns that show up most, steps for one boundary to set next week starting with the lowest-stakes person, and a quote with the opening line for that conversation.

tools.title: Guilt talk-down
tools.subtitle: The spiral after you held the line

inputs.label: What's going round your head
inputs.placeholder: I'm selfish, she'll never forgive me, I should just call and say yes

tools.prompt: Thoughts after holding a boundary: {feeling}. Text with a calm reality-check (3–4 sentences, no toxic positivity), a table (Thought | Distortion | Fairer version), a checklist for the next 24 hours (no undoing texts, one grounding action, one kind thing for yourself), and a callout on when persistent guilt or fear suggests talking to a therapist.

disclaimer: Coaching, not therapy. If you ever feel unsafe, controlled or afraid of someone close to you, contact a domestic-abuse helpline or emergency services.
